title: Introduction to quadratic equations and graphs
summary: Solving quadratic equations with the Null Factor Law, quadratic word problems, and sketching parabolas: dilations, reflections, translations and intercept form.

cards.title: Quadratic equations
cards.rule: Null Factor Law: if \(ab = 0\), then \(a = 0\) or \(b = 0\).
cards.note: A quadratic can have two, one or no solutions.

cards.title: Solving \(ax^2 + bx = 0\) and \(x^2 = d\)
cards.rule: Take out the common factor. For \(x^2 = d\), remember \(\pm\).

cards.title: Solving \(x^2 + bx + c = 0\)
cards.rule: Make one side 0, factorise, then use the Null Factor Law.

cards.title: Using quadratics to solve problems
cards.rule: Write an equation, solve it, then reject answers that don't make sense.
lines: A rectangle is 3 m longer than it is wide, area 40 m²: \(x(x + 3) = 40\)
Width can't be \(-8\), so it's 5 m by 8 m

cards.title: The parabola
cards.rule: \(y = x^2\) is a parabola. It has a turning point and an axis of symmetry.

cards.title: Dilations and reflections
cards.rule: \(y = ax^2\): a bigger \(|a|\) makes it narrower; a negative \(a\) flips it upside down.

cards.title: Translations
cards.rule: \(y = (x - h)^2 + k\) has turning point \((h, k)\).
cards.tip: the sign of \(h\) flips: \((x + 1)\) moves left 1.

cards.title: Intercept form
cards.rule: \(y = (x - a)(x - b)\) crosses the x-axis at \(a\) and \(b\). The turning point is halfway between.
